I have farmed these 28 mu in Quzhou County for 40 years. I am 58 now, and my hands know this soil better than any book. My household has four mouths, and my well gives us water when the sky does not. I do not chase fancy ideas. I stick with what has put food on the table and paid for my children's schooling.

My backbone is the wheat-maize rotation on 20 mu. That will never change. The remaining 8.1 mu I spread across cotton for cash, soybean and mungbean for extra income and to keep the soil alive, spinach for the county market, and a small patch of chrysanthemum that my wife dries for tea and sells to the medicine buyer.

For wheat, I plant an improved variety in early October. I rotary till the field and lay down base fertilizer. I top-dress urea at jointing, irrigate four times through the winter and spring, and spray herbicide plus fungicide two or three times. I expect around 520 kg per mu.

After wheat harvest in early June, there is no time to waste. I plant hybrid maize directly with no-tillage seeding. Maize is hungry, so I give it plenty of nitrogen and side-dress at the big trumpet stage. Three irrigations and two sprays are enough. In a normal year I get 600 kg per mu.

Cotton sits on 4 mu. I rotary till in spring, plant hybrid seed, and feed it heavy potassium because cotton is greedy for potash. I irrigate four times and spray five times for bollworm and aphids. I look for about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Soybean takes 2 mu. I use an improved variety. It fixes its own nitrogen, so I only give it a little N, but plenty of phosphorus and potassium. Two irrigations and two pesticide applications. I expect 170 kg per mu.

Mungbean is on 1.5 mu. Short season, low fuss. I rotary till, apply small amounts of fertilizer, irrigate twice, spray twice, and harvest about 100 kg per mu.

Spinach is 0.4 mu by the house. I grow it through autumn and winter for the market. It needs frequent water and some spray for leaf spot. Rotary tillage and heavy organic fertilizing. I cut it twice and get roughly 2,000 kg per mu.

Chrysanthemum is just 0.2 mu. I plant it in spring, tend it through summer, and pick the flowers in autumn. I rotary till, give it balanced fertilizer with extra potassium, irrigate five times, and spray four times for mildew and insects. Dried flowers should yield about 130 kg per mu.

This is my year. I do not gamble. I farm.
